newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin tells rivals to stop Chechnya bickering.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin tells rivals to stop Chechnya bickering.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Tuesday told rivals in the Kremlin and the government to stop bickering over their positions on breakaway Chechnya, press spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said.

He told a news conference that Yeltsin had ordered premier Viktor Chernomyrdin, security tsar Alexander Lebed and Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov to reach a consensus on Chechnya before closed parliamentary hearings on Tuesday. "As far as I know this order has been carried out," he said.

"The president is concerned by elements of confrontation on the public political stage...between members of the same team and in connection with this Boris Nikolayevich (Yeltsin) ordered the prime minister, the Security Council secretary and the interior minister to agree their position before closed hearings start in the State Duma on the Chechen problems," he said.
The Duma was debating Chechnya on Tuesday but participants said they did not expect any strong statements on the issue.

Security Council secretary Lebed signed a peace deal with Chechen separatist leaders on August 31. Russia promised to withdraw troops and both sides agreed to postpone a decision on the region's future political status for five years.

Other officials, including Kulikov, have criticised the deal, insisting Chechnya must remain part of Russia. On Monday Yeltsin named Lebed as the head of a team to lead further talks with the Chechen separatists.
